# Bell · November 6 engineering cleanup

**Completed: reproducible build validation that preserves a developer's existing output.** Engineering advances while human recruitment remains unbooked. The game generated by this cleanup is byte-identical to staged candidate **0.1.0**; no new candidate or official release is created.

| Area | Change | Actual outcome |
|---|---|---|
| Build command | `node build.mjs --output FILE` writes an explicit isolated output; default command remains compatible | Two isolated outputs match the prior build and staged candidate byte for byte |
| Validation | Static checks build in temporary locations; an existing local distribution is compared without being replaced | Clean checkouts remain clean; stale output fails and is preserved for diagnosis |
| Build anchors | Every inline replacement requires exactly one source anchor | Missing/duplicate anchors reject before touching output; literal JavaScript dollar sequences remain intact |
| Test ownership | A dependency-free build-contract suite joins the existing pure-rule tests | 25 reported Node tests passed, including all 15 existing rule tests |
| Current documentation | README describes ignored generated output, current HTTP setup, module ownership and next engineering work | Historical notes and study evidence retain their original dates and bytes |

[Verification and before/after results](VERIFICATION.md) · [Portable results](verification.json) · [Current developer commands](../../../README.md#tests)

## Current milestone and next goal

The clean-checkout build contract is ready for branch CI: run `node --test tests/*.test.cjs` and `python3 tests/check_static.py` without creating a default distribution. The next engineering goal is to wire those commands into an independent branch CI job and add browser smoke only on a supported runner. That CI integration remains planned; this report does not claim it exists. Source, rules, build tooling and evidence can be improved before recruitment completes.

Keep one owner for `js/engine.js`; narrative/content work uses `js/data.js`; pure-rule work uses `js/echo-time.js` and `js/square-event.js`; build and QA changes use `build.mjs` and `tests/`. Shared-state or content-contract changes need the integrator's agreed boundary before parallel implementation. No gameplay or rules-copy correction was selected in this cleanup.

## Human release work remains separate

The [November 5 facilitator kit](../readiness-2026-11-05/FACILITATOR-SETUP.md) still governs the same frozen candidate/reference and links to blank recording forms. Six actual people, balanced first-build order, at least 120 seconds of neutral recall, physical checks and independent human approval remain pending. No people or dates were supplied by the automated work.

Retain the November 11 candidate freeze, November 16 go/no-go and November 20 conditional launch cutoffs. Missing human evidence means the game stays staged; it does not stop independent engineering preparation. The original managed-browser access issue remains separate from the supported same-host HTTP route.
